instructions.title: Add your US game data before Play
instructions.instruction: Open the new runtime folder and copy your own US Ace Combat 6 Xbox 360 disc image beside ac6recomp.exe as AC6.iso, or put your extracted game files in assets with assets/default.xex. Keep your original copy separately. Europe and Japan are not supported. Choose Play after adding the files; this portable package has no installer. The game checks the disc title identity, but Portcove does not verify a retail-edition checksum for this upstream setup route. Optional own DLC belongs in dlc; title-update data is a separate upstream input, not a runtime update.

instructions.title: Keep your saves and settings
instructions.instruction: Saves and the default texture-mod profile use your Windows Documents/ac6recomp folder. Keep a separate backup of that folder before changing versions. Runtime settings and keyboard bindings sit beside the player in ac6recomp.toml and ac6_input.toml; use forward slashes in TOML paths. Runtime caches and logs also appear beside the player. If Windows cannot resolve Documents, the upstream relative ac6recomp fallback stays beside the player. Custom data, disc, DLC, log, mod and diagnostic locations remain yours to preserve separately. Close the game before changing runtime files; older versions may not read newer saves.

instructions.title: Know this release’s limits
instructions.instruction: Upstream requires Windows 10/11 x64, AVX2 and a Direct3D 12-capable GPU. This experimental release has known performance and rendering limits; Portcove gameplay and minimum-system observations remain unqualified.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: Player supplies own US Xbox360 ISO as AC6.iso or extracted assets/default.xex before explicit Play. Upstream probes title ID 0x4E4D07D1, not a Portcove retail-edition checksum. Europe/Japan unsupported by upstream. Own DLC and title updates retain separate identities. Default saves/mods/dumps use Documents/ac6recomp, outside Core backups; preserve separately. No game/original/helper execution.
setup_data.persistence_evidence: Exact source writes: main.cpp boot.log, keyboard default ac6_input.toml, SDK ReXApp config/ISO/assets/DLC roots and shader cache, core logging rotation, diag_crash_handler crash timestamp, PAC dump/probe output roots. Documents failure yields relative ac6recomp folder, retained in declared paths. Settings save directly to the exact TOML path. Custom paths and default external profile remain outside managed backup; runtime rollback does not rewind external saves.

instructions.title: Use the complete Windows player
instructions.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP includes mc2.exe, its libraries and game data. Keep the complete package together. For an existing copy, select mc2.exe in the extracted mc2-win64 folder and use that folder as the working directory. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. instructions.title: Back up the external saves
instructions.instruction: Normal saves use .mechcommander2/savegame under your Windows user-profile folder. Linux uses that path under XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set, otherwise HOME. Close the game and back up that external user-data folder separately. Keep options.cfg, options.cfg.old, orgprefs.cfg, data/multiplayer and any custom data locations with the copy you use. External profiles and custom paths are outside Portcove backups.

instructions.title: Keep an existing copy recoverable
instructions.instruction: For a copy you registered yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player separately and keep the working copy. Follow upstream guidance for settings and custom content; copying old generated texture or geometry caches over a new package can replace its new files. Registration leaves every external file untouched.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: The official Windows x64 package includes its game data and needs no original-file import or build. Portcove manages compatible runtime replacements and preserves local options.cfg, options.cfg.old, orgprefs.cfg and custom multiplayer data. Saves are external: back up your Windows user-profile folder/.mechcommander2/savegame separately; Portcove backups and runtime rollback do not include those saves. Generated texture and geometry caches, shader dumps and diagnostic files stay with each runtime version and are not carried into its replacement. Custom script output or custom data locations need separate preservation; unknown additions can block replacement until preserved. Runtime rollback carries current declared settings/custom data and does not rewind saves or guarantee older software can read newer data.

instructions.title: Prepare a permitted copy with upstream setup
instructions.instruction: For existing permitted copies of reNut and its setup tools, point NutStaller’s install folder at your player and use 3. Pick ISO + extract with your own USA Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts Xbox 360 ISO. This prepares game data and renut.cfg without downloading another runtime. instructions.title: Register the prepared player
instructions.instruction: On Windows choose the prepared renut.exe and its containing folder; on Linux choose the prepared renut.AppImage with its matching folder. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. Keep NutStaller for upstream updates, controls, Workshop and save tools. The Linux player and extraction helper have separate system requirements in upstream instructions; the reviewed launcher documents glibc 2.38 for the player and 2.34 for its extraction helper. If setting up the player manually, its first-run path wizard asks for your existing game and user-data folders.

instructions.title: Keep original files, saves and settings recoverable
instructions.instruction: You or upstream provide runtime updates. Close the game before using NutStaller to back up or to update to another release you have permission to acquire. Its normal user-data folder is Documents/renut on Windows and XDG_DATA_HOME/renut (normally ~/.local/share/renut) on Linux. Keep renut.cfg and renut.toml too: next to the Windows player, or in the Linux user-data folder. Retain your original ISO, prepared game folder, custom user-data paths, mods, and NutStaller configuration separately. Portcove external registration leaves these files untouched and supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

instructions.title: Select your own Banjo-Tooie ROM on first Play
instructions.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own NTSC-U 1.0 big-endian .z64 Banjo-Tooie ROM when asked. The upstream player requires SHA-256 9ec37fba6890362eba86fb855697a9cff1519275531b172083a1a6a045483583 and stores its own profile copy. The Windows ZIP has no installer. If Windows reports a missing runtime DLL, use the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 Redistributable linked in the packaged README; no helper runs automatically.

instructions.title: Keep your saves and settings
instructions.instruction: Saves, settings, copied ROM, logs, cache and RT64 texture packs use %LOCALAPPDATA%/BanjoTooieScurvyDogPort. Keep a separate backup; do not share the whole profile because it contains your ROM. On first start only, if this destination does not exist, the game can copy selected Alpha 4/4.1 data from BanjoTooieEncore while leaving the old profile unchanged. Close the old game first; the copies do not synchronize. An existing destination, even empty, wins. A failed copy can leave an unused .migrating-… folder; preserve it and consult the upstream recovery instructions before retrying. Alpha 3 save import asks once if there is no current save; Alpha 3 settings and practice states are not carried over. Texture packs are experimental; code mods and ROM patches are unsupported.

instructions.title: Know this release’s limits
instructions.instruction: This is an upstream alpha: distant geometry, aspect sizing, shadows, animation and lost-focus controller behavior have documented limitations; the upstream has not verified the whole game. Portcove gameplay and populated save restoration remain unqualified.

instructions.title: Build the Mac app with upstream setup
instructions.instruction: On an Apple Silicon Mac, use PadMint 0.5.1 or newer with Xcode and your own Mario Kart Wii PAL RMCP01 revision 0 disc. Choose Mario Kart Wii and This Mac, then move the resulting KartPad.app to Applications. Upstream lists macOS 14 or newer and describes the Mac version as experimental. Follow the linked guide if PadMint cannot download its tools or does not show This Mac; keep your existing game files and certificate verification.

instructions.title: Reuse your prepared game files
instructions.instruction: When KartPad first opens, select your own extracted game data. The linked Mac guide shows how to copy the matching version’s prepared disc folder from PadMint into a location you will keep, so you do not need to prepare it again. Retro Rewind needs the matching compiled version and its separate full data pack; keep the whole enclosing data folder because it can also contain saves. Building, importing and opening the app remain explicit upstream steps.

instructions.title: Keep saves when replacing the app
instructions.instruction: For newer Mac versions, build another app with PadMint, quit the current app and replace it through upstream’s instructions. Original settings and saves live in ~/Library/Application Support/KartPad; graphics caches are in ~/Library/Caches/KartPad. Keep Retro Rewind’s selected data folder too. The ready-made Mac downloads from 0.7.9 through 0.7.13 remain historical alternatives and no longer receive updates. Android uses its own APK and updater; iPhone/iPad use the separate PadMint and signing route. Portcove does not run PadMint, sign Apple apps, manage these bundles or back up their external data.

instructions.title: Keep upstream updates and your data together

The reviewed portable.txt keeps normal saves/cache in userdata; custom game-data/profile locations need a separate backup. Portcove leaves the external files untouched and supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

instructions.title: Select your ICO disc on first Play
instructions.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own ICO European SCES-50760, Japanese SCPS-11003 or Korean SCPS-56001 disc image when asked. Use ISO, CHD, or BIN with its matching CUE; the US disc is not supported. Keep the image outside the runtime folder. The game verifies and extracts its data on first launch (about 1 GB); later launches use that extracted copy. Keep your original image available if a future data-format change requires extraction again.

instructions.title: Keep saves with this portable copy
instructions.instruction: The official portable download enables portable=1 and keeps saves, settings and extracted disc data in userdata beside the player. Windows puts the player in x64; Linux puts it at the archive root. Back up userdata/memcard for saves, and use userdata/memcard2 for an optional second card. With portable=0 or an unwritable portable folder, data instead uses the upstream user-profile folder. Preserve that folder separately. Texture/model packs go in the documented textures/models folders. Close the game and preserve your current data before replacing a runtime; older versions may not read newer saves.

instructions.title: Other upstream platforms
instructions.instruction: The upstream project also publishes Apple-silicon macOS bundles, ARM Linux and mobile packages. Follow its platform guide for those copies; their setup and data locations differ from these Windows x64 and Linux x64 portable archives.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: Explicit first Play opens the upstream picker for the player's own EU SCES-50760, Japan SCPS-11003 or Korea SCPS-56001 ISO/CHD/BIN+CUE. US is unsupported. Upstream verifies disc identity/content and extracts user data, not a replacement runtime. Original image stays external and available for a future archive-format re-extraction; no original game input was acquired. ICO_ARCHIVE_VERSION1 / extractor major1 defines current cached-data acceptance.
setup_data.persistence_evidence: Both inspected archives set portable=1. Paths are executable-relative, matching Windows x64 subfolder and Linux root via existing Core behavior. userdata holds extracted disc archives, config.toml(+temporary), memory cards, screenshots, local achievements and pipeline cache. Exact ini.tmp retains interrupted atomic settings writes. Models/textures hold reviewed player packs and developer dump locations. Packaged overlaps are mutable ini and README placeholders, with no selected executable or runtime-code overlap. Use userdata/memcard2; custom paths, portable=0 and profile fallback stay outside Core backup ownership.

instructions.title: Add your own Descent 3 data before Play
instructions.instruction: Before Play, open the new runtime folder and copy only the original data from your own patched Descent 3 1.4 installation: d3.hog, extra.hog, extra13.hog, and missions/d3.mn3, d3_2.mn3, d3voice1.hog, d3voice2.hog and training.mn3. Keep the old installation intact. Add merc.hog and missions/merc.mn3 only if you own Mercenary; the upstream also recognizes the Steam extra1.hog expansion layout. For multiplayer, follow the packaged README for your own netgames directory and missions/Fury.mn3 and bedlam.mn3; movies are optional. Do not copy old top-level executables or DLLs over this runtime. Then choose Play. This ZIP has no installer; Portcove does not verify a retail-edition checksum for this upstream setup route.

instructions.title: Keep a separate backup of your Saved Games profile
instructions.instruction: Normal saves, pilots, demos, screenshots and temporary scripts use Windows Saved Games/Piccu Engine. The SDL configuration is Saved Games/Piccu Engine/PiccuEngine.registry, including when portable mode is used. Back up that external profile separately before changing runtime versions; older versions may not read newer data. Keep your original HOG files, missions, netgames and movies available separately too.

instructions.title: Keep customized copies separate
instructions.instruction: Adding piccu_portable, custom -setdir/-tempdir arguments or failure to resolve Saved Games can place player data and generated DLL caches in the runtime folder. An early startup crash can also leave a dump beside the player. Close the game and preserve your actual player-data locations before changing a customized copy. Do not copy generated script caches into another engine version; follow upstream instructions when changing storage modes.

instructions.title: Choose this Preview deliberately
instructions.instruction: This optional Windows Preview is the upstream SDL prototype, with fixes for pilot-control loading and input issues. Some settings do not import from older Piccu versions, and switching fullscreen/windowed can show a stray cursor. The stable v1.2.2 upstream copy remains available through the release list or an existing installation; it has separate known control issues. The player is Win32 and can run on 64-bit Windows through Windows compatibility support. Other platforms, gameplay, minimum Windows versions and populated-save restoration are not qualified here.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: Own patched Descent3 1.4 original HOG/mission data copied into a separate runtime before explicit Play. Copy only listed data, never blanket-import old top-level binaries. Normal pilots/saves/demos/screenshots/temp DLL extraction use external Saved Games/Piccu Engine. SDL config is external Saved Games/Piccu Engine/PiccuEngine.registry even in portable mode. Portcove backup does not cover that profile. Runtime rollback keeps current declared originals and does not rewind external data.
setup_data.persistence_evidence: docs/readme.md specifies originals/optional expansion/multiplayer/movie copies; init.cpp reads Steam extra1.hog too, uses User_directory/custom/cache for generated scripts; OsirisLoadandBind.cpp extracts to that temporary location and removes those scripts; sdldatabase.cpp fixes registry location to Saved Games. Do not declare generated cache as transferable player data.

instructions.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
instructions.instruction: After downloading, open the download folder and run the TRX Windows Installer yourself when ready. Choose a new TRX folder, separate from your current working copy and original games. Select the packs you want and provide your own supported original Steam, GOG or disc installations. Upstream setup maps their files into the combined games folders. The installer needs the x64 .NET 8 Desktop Runtime; follow its upstream instructions if that prerequisite is missing.

instructions.title: Choose the installed player
instructions.instruction: When setup finishes, choose TRX.exe from the folder you installed into, using that folder as its working directory. Choose the game pack in TRX. Save the launch details in Portcove, then choose Play separately. The downloaded installer is not the game executable.

instructions.title: Keep the working copy when updating
instructions.instruction: You or upstream own runtime updates and the combined game folders. Prepare a new version separately and keep the current copy until it works. The upstream installer overwrites target files and removes unchecked game packs, so do not point it at your only working copy. Keep separate copies of saves, cfg settings and any custom data. Portcove registration does not back up, roll back or delete this external tree. The Windows/Linux manual ZIP route is also available upstream; follow its exact original-file mapping rather than copying an entire disc into the player folder.

instructions.title: Choose your own ROM and BIOS in the game
instructions.instruction: The Windows ZIP is ready to open after extraction; it has no installer or player build step. Keep its DLLs, assets, any supplied mods and overlay_toolchain together. Finish setup with MarioKartSuperCircuitRecomp.exe, then choose Play explicitly. In the game’s launcher, select your own Mario Kart: Super Circuit USA, AMKE revision 0 ROM and retail GBA BIOS, then Play. The expected ROM SHA-1 is 9d327c030c3e2d9007990518594f70c3340ac56f; the retail BIOS SHA-1 is 300c20df6731a33952ded8c436f7f186d25d3492. The game remembers valid selections. The tcc programs are internal compiler helpers, not the player; Portcove does not run them during setup discovery.

instructions.title: Keep the saves and settings you actually use
instructions.instruction: By default, cartridge saves use the selected ROM’s name with .sav, and save-state slots use the same name with .state1 through .state10, beside that ROM. Keep a separate copy of this folder; a save path shown in the launcher is not proof that the save moved there. Also preserve config.ini, keybinds.ini, rom.cfg, bios.cfg, your mod choices and any player-added mods beside the executable. Custom --save/--save-path or --state-dir choices change the save locations. Older builds may not read newer states or saves. Portcove registration preserves these externally owned files; it does not back up or restore them.

instructions.title: Keep your working copy when updating
instructions.instruction: Updates come from the upstream project. Extract a new release into a separate folder and keep the current copy usable while checking it. Keep each release’s own DLLs, packaged mods and overlay_toolchain; do not overlay the old runtime folder onto the new one. The game can generate native code in recomp_cache during Play. Keep that old cache with the old copy and let the new release start with its own cache, rather than transferring generated DLLs. Transfer only compatible player settings, saves and mods using the matching upstream instructions, then change the registered player when ready. These previews remain experimental; downloading or registering one does not establish full-game compatibility.

instructions.title: Linux and optional netplay
instructions.instruction: Upstream also publishes a Linux x86-64 AppImage. Follow its Linux instructions, make that AppImage executable and open it deliberately; do not treat it as the Windows ZIP. Its launcher selects your own matching ROM and BIOS. For optional two-player link-cable netplay, use the same release and ROM on both sides, choose the actual save file before connecting, and keep a backup. Higher resolution and widescreen are optional; upstream recommends at most 4x internal resolution. Portcove does not qualify Linux execution or a network session here.

instructions.title: Choose your own ROM and BIOS in the game
instructions.instruction: The Windows ZIP is ready to open after extraction; it has no installer or player build step. Keep its DLLs, assets, any supplied mods and overlay_toolchain together. Finish setup with DragonBallZBuusFuryRecomp.exe, then choose Play explicitly. In the game’s launcher, select your own Dragon Ball Z: Buu’s Fury USA, BG3E revision 0 ROM and retail GBA BIOS, then Play. The expected ROM SHA-1 is f1c4b07554d2a3b1ad2f325307051e775ce68087; the retail BIOS SHA-1 is 300c20df6731a33952ded8c436f7f186d25d3492. The game remembers valid selections. The tcc programs are internal compiler helpers, not the player; Portcove does not run them during setup discovery.

instructions.title: Keep the saves and settings you actually use
instructions.instruction: By default, cartridge saves use the selected ROM’s name with .sav, and save-state slots use the same name with .state1 through .state10, beside that ROM. Keep a separate copy of this folder; a save path shown in the launcher is not proof that the save moved there. Also preserve config.ini, keybinds.ini, rom.cfg, bios.cfg, your mod choices and any player-added mods beside the executable. Custom --save/--save-path or --state-dir choices change the save locations. Older builds may not read newer states or saves. Portcove registration preserves these externally owned files; it does not back up or restore them.

instructions.title: Keep your working copy when updating
instructions.instruction: Updates come from the upstream project. Extract a new release into a separate folder and keep the current copy usable while checking it. Keep each release’s own DLLs, packaged mods and overlay_toolchain; do not overlay the old runtime folder onto the new one. The game can generate native code in recomp_cache during Play. Keep that old cache with the old copy and let the new release start with its own cache, rather than transferring generated DLLs. Transfer only compatible player settings, saves and mods using the matching upstream instructions, then change the registered player when ready. These previews remain experimental; downloading or registering one does not establish full-game compatibility.

Before starting a game, Settings > Saves can import a checked compatible save and keeps the previous file alongside as .pre-import.bak. That is an upstream import safeguard, not a complete backup or compatibility promise for arbitrary emulator saves. Preserve app data using the upstream Android methods before uninstalling or clearing storage. For an affected Adreno launch crash, the guide offers disabling Framebuffer Effects before selecting an optional custom driver. Portcove does not install drivers, update the APK or back up its profile.

Upstream requires Android 9+ and Vulkan; a physical controller is useful but current releases also have touch controls. Saves and settings share the app-scoped profile. instructions.title: Choose the game you want to play
instructions.instruction: For 64-bit Windows, use the official stable portable ZIP in a separate folder. It contains three different players: RedAlert.exe for Red Alert, TiberianDawn.exe for Tiberian Dawn, and Dune2000.exe for Dune 2000. Choose that game executable when finishing setup; OpenRA.Server and OpenRA.Utility are not the normal players. Portcove leaves this choice to you and does not run a discovered helper. Alternatively use the upstream Windows installer, the game-specific Linux AppImage, or the macOS disk image, then register the prepared player. An AppImage or disk image needs its own upstream platform instructions, not ZIP extraction.

instructions.title: Let your chosen game finish its own content setup
instructions.instruction: Choose Play explicitly, then follow that player’s content installation screen. It can offer upstream downloads or import from your own original game media; available content differs between Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn and Dune 2000. Portcove does not run these content tools during discovery or supply original media.

instructions.title: Keep the OpenRA profile and current copy
instructions.instruction: Updates come from OpenRA. Install a new release separately and keep your current copy usable while checking it; stable releases and playtests are different choices. Saves, settings, downloaded content, maps, replays and screenshots normally use %APPDATA%/OpenRA on Windows, ~/.config/openra on Linux, or ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA on macOS. An existing legacy profile may be reused. A Support directory beside the engine, or an explicit support-directory setting, changes this location. Back up the profile you actually use separately; Portcove does not manage this runtime or promise Backup/Rollback for it. An older engine may not read newer saves/mods. Custom mods use their own matching engine/runtime instructions.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: Explicit Play launches the chosen game's own content-install screen. Original media or optional upstream downloads stay under upstream consent; discovery runs nothing. Default profile AppData/OpenRA, Linux .config/openra, macOS Library/Application Support/OpenRA; existing legacy fallback and sibling Support/custom override can change actual location. Back up the actual profile separately; engine/mod/version compatibility is upstream-owned.

instructions.title: Prepare your own disc before Play
instructions.instruction: Before Play, prepare game-data beside the new player from your own Ratchet & Clank (2002) NTSC-U SCUS-97199 version 1.00 disc. Use a 2048-byte-sector .iso; BIN, CHD and another region are not accepted by this extractor. Open the installed runtime folder and deliberately run its bundled rerac-extract.exe on Windows, or ./rerac-extract on Linux/macOS: identify --iso "<your ISO>", then extract --iso "<your ISO>" --out game-data, then verify --out game-data. Wait for successful completion and verification; allow about 4.5 GB for extracted disc data plus prepared caches. Keep the complete runtime folder and its assets/shaders together. Then choose Play. Portcove never runs this extractor during discovery. The upstream runtime refuses missing, incomplete or incompatible extraction; wait for successful extraction and verification before Play.

instructions.title: Use the guided launcher when you prefer
instructions.instruction: For guided ISO selection, progress, verification, re-extraction and version management, use the official ReRAC Launcher linked by Open setup guide. Its published Windows MSI, Linux AppImage and macOS disk images are separate from these game ZIPs. Follow its Version Management and Install via ISO flow, then register your prepared player with its real data directory, or register the launcher deliberately if you want its own interface. That copy’s runtime updates belong to the launcher. The project’s older README statement that nothing has been released does not describe the currently published launcher packages. Mod management is planned, not a delivered feature.

instructions.title: Keep a separate backup of your memory card
instructions.instruction: Normal memory-card saves, settings and the crash log are outside the runtime: %APPDATA%/rerac on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rerac or ~/.config/rerac on Linux, and ~/Library/Application Support/rerac on macOS. Back up the profile you actually use separately. A custom RC_SAVE_DIR or RC_SETTINGS_FILE changes it. The launcher’s movable data/version/log folder can be different from the engine’s save/settings folder; preserve both when using it. Older versions may not read newer saves. Keep your original ISO and current working copy before re-extraction or changing versions.

instructions.title: Build your copy for Apple Silicon Mac
instructions.instruction: Use upstream PadMint 0.5.5 or newer on an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode. Choose SunPad, your own Super Mario Sunshine USA revision 0 GMSE01 raw ISO/GCM, and This Mac. Move the SunPad.app ZIP output to Applications after extracting it. The linked guide also provides a manual source-build route. Published iPhone/iPad app shells do not contain the translated game code and cannot play by themselves; they are not Mac packages.

instructions.title: Choose the original image in SunPad
instructions.instruction: Open your prepared Mac app when ready. Choose the supported image in its launcher and select Extract and Play. Upstream owns that extraction, generated module and launch. Other regions, revisions and modified or compressed images are not established by this route. Portcove does not run the builder, obtain game files or sign Apple applications.

instructions.title: Keep the app data when updating
instructions.instruction: Build a newer app separately and follow upstream’s replacement instructions while keeping your current working copy. Mac configuration, extracted game data, saves, logs and controller profiles are under ~/Library/Application Support/SunPad; keep a separate backup before replacing or re-preparing anything. iPhone/iPad signing identity and experimental Apple TV’s purgeable storage have separate rules in the platform guides. Portcove does not manage bundle replacement, back up this external data or promise runtime rollback. Check upstream’s known issues before replacing a working app.

setup_data.reviewed_boundary: Current source/README route builds a local arm64 SunPad.app through PadMint0.5.5+ or manual Xcode pipeline from own GMSE01r0 raw ISO/GCM, then upstream launcher extracts and plays. Published IPA shells lack game code and are not Mac runtimes. Unsupported app-bundle handling and owner-generated module pipeline do not fit native-portable managed replacement. All Mac user/config/generated state in Application Support/SunPad remains external. iOS signing and tvOS purgeable data stay separate.

instructions.title: Select your own Glover ROM on first Play
instructions.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own unmodified Glover USA revision 0 ROM when the game asks. The launcher accepts .z64, .n64 and .v64 byte order for this 8 MiB NGVE cartridge (canonical SHA-1 270be17b3c8da9b88a7b99c2a545b0bce16837f4). The published Windows player needs no game build or separate installer. Configure controls in the launcher or press F1/Escape while playing; use its Mods page for compatible mods and separate mod profiles.

instructions.title: Keep your saves and mod profiles safe
instructions.instruction: Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Glover-R. Keep a separate backup of that profile before changing versions; an older runtime may not read newer data. Optional custom configuration and developer paths need their own backup. Keep customized existing copies registered with their own launch details.

instructions.title: Linux uses the upstream AppImage route
instructions.instruction: Use the Linux x86-64 AppImage, or extract the Linux Portable archive and deliberately run Launch-Glover-R.sh. That archive contains an AppImage and wrapper, rather than a bare player with ordinary libraries. The wrapper uses AppImage extraction mode when a normal AppImage launch is unavailable. Steam Deck uses its separate x86-64 package and START-GLOVER-R.sh. Linux saves/settings normally use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/glover-r or ~/.config/glover-r; preserve that actual profile separately. Follow upstream updates for this copy; the Windows managed route does not manage the Linux wrapper or infer device/gameplay support.

instructions.title: Let the upstream launcher prepare your own game
instructions.instruction: The recommended Windows download is the upstream lawn/Z3R Launcher setup package. Open that installer deliberately after downloading, then use its guided preparation. Install its published package for your platform, choose your own clean USA A Link to the Past .sfc, and follow its setup/extract/build steps. The Windows setup package includes the lightweight Git/Python/TCC/SDL2 toolkit; choosing a separate MSBuild route needs its own build tools. Linux and macOS use their matching upstream dependency guide. Portcove does not install these tools or run the launcher during discovery. When setup finishes, register the prepared zelda3.exe on Windows or native zelda3 player on Linux/macOS with its project folder as the working directory, then choose Play explicitly.

instructions.title: Keep the generated assets and player data together
instructions.instruction: Keep the complete prepared project, your original ROM, zelda3_assets.dat, zelda3.user.ini overrides, saves, custom sprites/shaders/MSU packs, and any randomizer YAML, seed/spoiler files or selected feature-asset folders separately backed up. The game tries zelda3.user.ini before zelda3.ini. Keep packaged defaults with their own release and use user overrides for personal settings. The native release ZIP supplies a player and SDL but no generated zelda3_assets.dat; copying that executable alone is not finished setup.

instructions.title: Regenerate matching assets when updating
instructions.instruction: Let the selected upstream launcher manage its own project setup and updates. The game’s guide requires asset regeneration after relevant executable/source, extraction-script, YAML or INI behavior changes. Copying an older generated asset file into a replacement runtime cannot satisfy that requirement. Preserve the old prepared copy and randomizer choices before regeneration; extracting clean ROM data after randomizing overwrites the randomized YAML. Portcove registers the prepared player without claiming Update, Backup or Rollback for these externally owned files. The related Python Z3R-Launcher and current lawn delivery are helpers for this same engine identity, not extra games.
